Define and save a cohort

Source: vignettes/articles/cohorts.Rmd
cohorts.Rmd
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

The examples use invented discharges. A code slot is a numbered column that holds one diagnosis or procedure code.

Match diagnosis and procedure codes 

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(
    heart_failure = list(regex = "I50[0-9]+", exclude = "I509")
  ) |>
  nis_flag_dx(principal_hf = "I50", position = "principal") |>
  nis_flag_pr(pci = "0270")

nis |> count(heart_failure, principal_hf, pci) |> collect()
#> # A tibble: 4 × 4
#>   heart_failure principal_hf pci       n
#>   <lgl>         <lgl>        <lgl> <dbl>
#> 1 TRUE          TRUE         TRUE     54
#> 2 FALSE         FALSE        FALSE    42
#> 3 TRUE          TRUE         FALSE    54
#> 4 FALSE         FALSE        TRUE     42

The default position checks all slots. Use position = "principal" for slot 1. A string such as "I50" matches a prefix. A regex matches the whole stored code. If you supply both, either can set the flag. Exclusions apply to individual matching codes, so another slot can still set the flag.

mixed <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2014:2016)) |>
  mutate(DX1 = if_else(
    (YEAR == 2014 | (YEAR == 2015 & DQTR < 4)) & HOSP_NIS %% 2L == 0L,
    "4280", DX1
  )) |>
  nis_flag_dx(hf = list(icd9 = "428", icd10 = "I50"), system = "both")
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:

#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Experimental: years before 2016 store ICD-9-CM codes in DX1, PR1, ... slots.
#> ℹ Flag them with `system = "icd9"`; 2015 mixes ICD-9 (Q1-Q3) and ICD-10 (Q4)
#>   slots.

mixed |> filter(YEAR == 2015) |> count(DQTR, hf) |> arrange(DQTR, hf) |> collect()

#>    DQTR hf        n

nis_attrition(mixed, adult = AGE >= 18, hf = hf, by_year = TRUE, .design = TRUE)

Supply separate definitions for each system when the source contains both slot sets. The example adds invented ICD-9 matches so you can see both systems in the quarter audit and follow eligibility counts across all three years. Check how your own code sets behave around the transition. Years and coding eras

Use CCSR categories or procedure days

The Clinical Classifications Software Refined (CCSR) groups ICD-10 codes into clinical categories.

nis |>
  nis_add_ccsr(position = "default", version = "2025.1") |>
  count(ccsr) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   ccsr       n
#>   <chr>  <dbl>
#> 1 CIR019   108
#> 2 RSP002    84

timing <- nis |> mutate(PRDAY1 = 0L, PRDAY2 = 1L)
nis_audit_prday(timing, pr = "0270")
#> # A tibble: 50 × 8
#>     YEAR  slot matched_slots known_day missing_day sentinel_invalid_day
#>    <int> <int>         <int>     <int>       <int>                <int>
#>  1  2019     1            48        48           0                    0
#>  2  2019     2             0         0           0                    0
#>  3  2019     3             0         0           0                    0
#>  4  2019     4             0         0           0                    0
#>  5  2019     5             0         0           0                    0
#>  6  2019     6             0         0           0                    0
#>  7  2019     7             0         0           0                    0
#>  8  2019     8             0         0           0                    0
#>  9  2019     9             0         0           0                    0
#> 10  2019    10             0         0           0                    0
#> # ℹ 40 more rows
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: absent_prday_column <int>, pct_known <dbl>
timing |>
  nis_flag_pr_timing(
    index_pr = list(prefix = "0270", exclude = "02703DZ"),
    outcome_pr = list(regex = "02L73.*"),
    relation = "after", missing_day = "indeterminate"
  ) |>
  count(outcome_post_index) |>
  collect()
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpdqWbY1/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   outcome_post_index     n
#>   <lgl>              <dbl>
#> 1 FALSE                168
#> 2 TRUE                  24

The bundled v2025.1 mappings can keep the same definitions across study years. position = "default" returns one inpatient category for the principal diagnosis. The example supplies invented procedure days. Timing uses the earliest known index day and accepts the same prefixes, full-code regular expressions, and exact exclusions as nis_flag_pr(). For system = "both", supply named icd9 and icd10 definitions for each procedure. Timing compares slots within the same code system. Audit procedure-day availability before interpreting an order.

Count eligibility steps and save the cohort 

flow <- nis_attrition(
  nis, adult = AGE >= 18, hf = heart_failure, by_year = TRUE, .design = TRUE
)
flow
#> # A tibble: 6 × 8
#>    YEAR  step criterion             n_unweighted n_dropped_unweighted n_weighted
#>   <int> <int> <chr>                        <int>                <int>      <dbl>
#> 1  2020     0 Valid design dischar…           96                   NA      114. 
#> 2  2020     1 adult                           96                    0      114. 
#> 3  2020     2 hf                              54                   42       62.4
#> 4  2019     0 Valid design dischar…           96                   NA      114. 
#> 5  2019     1 adult                           96                    0      114. 
#> 6  2019     2 hf                              54                   42       62.4
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: n_dropped_weighted <dbl>, pct_retained <dbl>

eligible <- nis_attrition_cohort(flow)
export <- nis |> mutate(stayDays = LOS)
path <- nis_write_cohort(export, !!eligible, tempfile(), keep = c(AGE, stayDays))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpdqWbY1/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(nis_open(path), keep = stayDays)
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpdqWbY1/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
summarise(design, total = survey_total(), mean_stay = survey_mean(stayDays))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 4
#>   total total_se mean_stay mean_stay_se
#>   <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1  125.     17.3      5.66        0.229

The flow counts remaining discharges after each criterion. The saved Parquet cohort retains the hospital structure used for variance. Open it without supplying a new cohort to nis_design(). Derived names such as stayDays keep their spelling when you reopen the saved cohort. Keep the code that defined your flags with the study.
